title: RTO holds up three school tour buses over loud sound systems, dance floors; 102 students put through anxious 4 hours
content: Kasaragod: The Motor Vehicles Department (MVD) held up an excursion by 102 Class XII students of St Jude's Higher Secondary School at Vellarikundu for nearly four hours after officers stopped three tourist buses over alleged illegal modifications, including loud sound systems, laser lights and dance floors. Vellarikundu Joint Regional Transport Officer AK Najeeb said the action followed complaints from two rival tour operators, who alleged that buses fitted with such modifications were getting trips while their own buses, which did not have these features, were being left out. The Joint RTO action triggered a confrontation involving school authorities, people's representatives and officials, but Najeeb stood his ground and let the buses go after filing a case against them for illegal modifications. The buses were scheduled to leave for Mysuru and Chikkamagaluru at 1 pm. However, officials led by the Joint RTO intervened as students boarded the buses, alleging the vehicles had unauthorised lighting and sound systems, including equipment that converted their passenger compartments into dance floors. Principal Fr Santhosh Peter told Onmanorama that he had informed the RTO about the excursion on November 12, six days before the scheduled departure. The application contained the registration numbers of all three buses, details of their drivers and other particulars of the trip, he said. "We gave all the details of the three buses and the drivers to the RTO," said Fr Peter. "But the officials came in the last minute to disrupt the trip," he said. The group had planned to reach Chikkamagaluru by 8 pm for dinner after a stopover at Belur in Karnataka's Hassan district, known for its Chennakeshava Temple and Hoysala architecture. The delay forced the school to revise the itinerary. "Now we will reach Chikkamagaluru only by 11 pm. So we rescheduled dinner to another place and dropped the sightseeing at Belur," said Fr Peter, who is accompanying the students. He alleged that the Joint RTO was unwilling to hear the school's explanation and threatened to seize all three buses over the modifications. Trikaripur MLA Sandeep Varier intervened and asked the officer to obtain an undertaking from the school and allow the children to proceed. However, Najeeb did not agree. The officials prepared a report, registered cases over the modifications and let the buses go for the tour. "But by then our children and their parents were mentally down and felt harassed," Fr Peter said. Local representatives, including Balal panchayat vice-president Raju Kattakkayam and ward member Shoby Joseph, along with representatives of various political parties, also reached the school after learning about the intervention. They sought an explanation from the officials, but the Joint RTO allegedly refused to engage with them and instructed his staff to proceed with action against the buses. According to Najeeb, the three buses were registered in the names of different individuals but were taken on lease and operated by one person. He said the buses had been fitted with high-powered speakers, woofers, additional lighting and dance-floor-style lighting arrangements, including coloured and laser lights. "We received complaints from two tourist bus operators from Vellarikundu itself. The modifications are patently illegal," he said. The officer said he had sent inspectors to examine the vehicles on Wednesday and personally went to the spot after noticing the buses playing loud music near his office. 'Not fitness certificates' Najeeb explained that there were two distinct fitness requirements: the regular fitness certificate establishing a vehicle's roadworthiness and a separate fitness inspection report required before it undertakes a school tour. The school did not submit the tour fitness certificates for the buses along with its applications, he said...
